findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, all in plain words. This is the page's strongest part.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The first section after the header is an error message. It shows none of the trace, cost or verdict that the lede promises, so the newcomer's first look at evidence is a failure. That hurts trust more than anything else on the page.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The title is about firstmate, but the lede is about Athena. A newcomer may not know which product the page is showing them until they read the third paragraph, which says this page is a study Athena made of another project.
This link is aimed at the owner, not a newcomer. It sits next to the Next step link and gives no context, so a stranger may think they are expected to make decisions.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The "Start here" section explains firstmate clearly and defines its terms before using them. A newcomer can say what firstmate does without reading the transition cards.
findings.source: Start here / What firstmate is: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker..."

findings.text: The States, Transitions and Counters sections are dense, specialist detail with many terms in each sentence. That makes sense for checking claims, but it is a lot to take in for a newcomer who only wants to judge what Athena can do.
findings.source: Transitions, t8 summary: "A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the source does not define the term. That is honest, but the newcomer is left with words used throughout the page that are never explained.
findings.source: Glossary, endpoint: "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint."; also "in scope": "this page gives no test for it"

findings.text: Next steps gives concrete actions: what to install first, how to install, and a first command to try. It is linked from the header, so a newcomer can find what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Each claim links to specific lines at a pinned commit. This shows the traceability the lede promises, even though the live job evidence above is missing.
findings.source: Claims and sources: "AGENTS.md:206-206" links to the pinned commit
